root_cause.text: The XFS xattr leaf freemap maintenance code in xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work can leave stale zero-length freemap entries with a nonzero base, causing the limited freemap array to contain overlapping/duplicate base records that later misdirect xattr allocation into the entries array.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “This code can leave behind a zero-length freemap entry with a nonzero base” and that later updates can produce “two entries with the same base but different sizes,” after which “a subsequent _leaf_add can then allocate xattr namevalue entries on top of the entries array”; the patch fixes this by clearing freemap[i].base when freemap[i].size == 0.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear stale base offsets from zero-length freemap entries to prevent overlapping freemap corruption during later attribute removal and recovery.
intent_record.what: A new conditional block was added inside xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work() after freemap size adjustment: if ichdr->freemap[i].size is 0 and ichdr->freemap[i].base is greater than 0, the code now resets ichdr->freemap[i].base to 0 and sets ichdr->holes to 1, along with a comment explaining why.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents zero-length freemap entries from retaining a nonzero base offset, which could cause later remove-path logic that matches on base address to misidentify free regions and create overlapping freemap entries. Marking holes ensures the leaf can be compacted and freemaps regenerated on a subsequent add.

grouping_result.intent: Clear stale base offsets from zero-length freemap entries to prevent overlapping freemap corruption during later attribute removal and recovery.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by clearing stale base values in zero-length freemap entries, preventing duplicate/overlapping freemap records that can later corrupt xattr allocation.

candidates.rationale: This is the only pre-fix statement shown in the vulnerable area. The root cause is missing freemap cleanup after consuming/freeing space; updating usedbytes without also clearing stale zero-length freemap base offsets allows invalid freemap records to persist.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement updates the leaf used-bytes accounting when adding the attribute entry, but in the vulnerable pre-fix code path it does so without also clearing stale zero-length freemap entries whose base offsets remain nonzero. That omission allows overlapping or duplicate freemap records to persist and later misdirect xattr allocation into the entries array.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains the freemap update logic at the end of xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work, which is exactly where the root cause occurs. The vulnerable construct is present in the loop at lines 1422-1426: `if (ichdr->freemap[i].base == tmp) { ichdr->freemap[i].base += sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t); ichdr->freemap[i].size -= sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t); }`. This code adjusts `base` and `size` when the entry array grows, but it does not handle the case where subtracting `sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t)` makes `ichdr->freemap[i].size` become zero. In that situation, the code leaves behind a zero-length freemap entry with a nonzero `base`, which matches the described root cause: stale zero-length freemap entries with nonzero base can remain and later overlap or duplicate other freemap records. There is no corrective handling here to clear the base, remove the record, or otherwise sanitize zero-sized freemap entries, so the fix is not present.
